subject: Request: Exec review for HelioTech multi-year prepay + ramp concession
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@heliotech.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliotech.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Initial proposal: multi-year prepay + ramp options (HelioTech)

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I attached two structured pricing options for a 3-year engagement where HelioTech prepays annually. Both options assume the same committed annual token volumes but different ramp schedules and discount timing.

Summary (high-level):
- Option A — Standard ramp: 30% discount Y1 (annual prepay), 20% Y2, 10% Y3; even consumption ramp across quarters.
- Option B — Aggressive initial concession: 45% discount Y1 (to help your FY26 budget), ramp to 25% Y2 and 15% Y3, with a volume guarantee and reporting cadence.

We can support Option B but it requires an executive exception and a non-standard ramp schedule in the SOW. Can you confirm which option your CFO prefers? If it’s Option B, I’ll escalate for sign-off and share the exception memo + SOW redline for legal.

Attachments: HelioTech_Proposed_Term_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx, 80KB)

Next step: your preference + any internal timing constraints (procurement signoff window).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0126

From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@heliotech.com>

Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: multi-year prepay + ramp options (HelioTech)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear options. Short answer: our CFO is pushing for the biggest possible saving in FY26 because of the product launch; that makes Option B attractive. Two asks from our side before we can route to legal/procurement:

1) Can you confirm the credit/refund mechanics if actual consumption is below guarantee in Y1?
2) We need a softer ramp (we expect volume to be backloaded in Q3/Q4). Can the 45% Y1 price apply to any usage up to the committed annual volume even if consumed later in the year?

If you can get an executive note supporting that concession we can start procurement review this week.

Thanks,
Daniel

Team —

Looping you in. HelioTech (strategic target in healthcare analytics) is asking for an aggressive first-year prepay concession (45% off list) plus the ability to apply that Y1 price across the annual committed volume even if consumption skews later in the year. They’re ready to prepay annually and sign a 3-year term, but procurement/legal will want our exception memo and clear refund/underspend mechanics.

Why I’m escalating: Option B closes faster but increases near-term revenue giveback. We can recover in Y2/Y3, but this is a non-standard ramp and requires exec exception + finance/recognition alignment. Key asks for decision:
- Approve one-time deviation to discount cadence (45% / 25% / 15%)?
- Approve flexible timing for Y1 discount to apply to annual committed volume regardless of quarter of consumption?
- Any constraints from finance / revenue recognition we should be aware of?

Attachments: RWI_Special_Pricing_Memo_20251115.pdf (pdf, 120KB), HelioTech_Proposed_Term_Schedule.xlsx

If you want, I can propose a middle ground (35% Y1 with a minimum quarterly consumption floor) but Helio prefers the full 45% to hit internal budget targets. Need a thumbs-up or suggested counter so I can respond to procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioTech asks for 45% Y1 concession — exec approval request

Marissa —

Thanks for the context and the memo. My read: HelioTech is strategically attractive, and a multi-year prepay helps our committed revenue. That said, 45% Y1 is outside our standard deviation for enterprise prepay concessions. Proposed counter (fast path to close):

- Offer: 35% discount Y1 if Helio signs within 7 business days and prepays for Y1.
- Conditioning: True-up clause at year-end — if consumption < 80% of committed annual volume, credit applied to Y2 at a capped rate (not cash refund).
- Flex ramp: allow Y1 price to apply to annual committed volume regardless of intra-year timing, but require a minimum quarterly floor of 15% of committed volume.

If Evelyn and Vivek are good with this we can present tonight. Prefer to avoid cash refunds; credits to future invoices keeps recognition cleaner.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks for the quick feedback and patience while we routed internally. We can meet you partway. Here’s our revised fast-close offer:

Proposed (final):
- 3-year term, annual prepay.
- Year 1: 35% discount (prepay required within 7 business days of executed SOW).
- Year 2: 22% discount; Year 3: 12% discount.
